name: AnyFrame

hlido_opinion.headline: A harness-agnostic platform for spinning up team agents inside Slack/Linear/GitHub — a clean concept and real SDK, but visibly pre-traction and crowded on differentiation.
hlido_opinion.body: AnyFrame's bet is that teams do not want to marry one coding harness: you build a named, sandboxed agent, bind it to a template and a runtime, and swap between Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or OpenCode without changing everything else. It triggers where people already work — a Slack message, a Linear ticket, a PR comment — and it ships an SDK ('pip install anyframe', TypeScript too) so agents can be created and run in a few lines. The harness-swappability and the trigger-where-you-work framing are the genuinely appealing ideas, and the free-to-try model (500 credits, no card) lowers the bar to evaluate. The caution flags are equally clear from the public surface: the product looks early — the in-page dashboard literally shows 'No agents yet', self-hosting is 'coming soon', and several of the flagship behaviours (browser 'hands and eyes', describe-and-preview) are shown as demos rather than proven; and the category is crowded, so 'any agent, any team, any tool' reads more as positioning than as a demonstrated moat. Worth watching, but this is an early platform to trial, not yet infrastructure to standardise on.

tier_rationale: STEADY (71) for a coherent concept (harness-agnostic team agents triggered in existing tools), a real SDK/API surface, and a low-friction free trial. Held near the band floor because the public surface shows a pre-traction product (empty dashboard, self-hosting "coming soon", demo-shown flagship features) in a crowded space where the differentiation is asserted rather than demonstrated.
what_it_does_well: Harness-agnostic by design — swap Claude Code / Cursor / Codex / OpenCode without re-tooling
Triggers inside existing workflows (Slack, Linear, GitHub PR/issue comments)
Real programmatic surface: Python and TypeScript SDKs to create and run agents in a few lines
Low-friction evaluation: 500 free credits, no credit card, pay-as-you-go after
Clear, honest FAQ (sandbox isolation, human-approval gating for risky/production actions)
what_it_fails_at: Visibly early: the in-product dashboard shows "No agents yet"; self-hosting/open-source is "coming soon"
Flagship capabilities (browser "hands and eyes", describe-and-preview) are presented as demos, not proven outcomes
Differentiation is asserted ("any agent, any team, any tool") in a crowded category without a demonstrated moat
No public reliability, security, or track-record evidence on the surface
best_for: Teams wanting to trial agents inside Slack/Linear/GitHub without committing to a single harness
Developers who want to script agent creation/runs via an SDK
Early adopters comfortable evaluating a pre-1.0 platform
not_recommended_for: Teams needing self-hosting or an on-prem story today (not yet available)
Buyers who need proven reliability before standardising on a platform
Anyone wanting a clearly differentiated, battle-tested orchestration layer now
red_flags: Product appears pre-traction (empty dashboard state, "coming soon" self-hosting) while marketing implies breadth — evaluate before depending on it
